findings.title: Fallback chain reads SiteSetting on every translation lookup
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] builds a new array by reading SiteSetting.default_locale and calling to_sym each time it is invoked. I18n consults the fallback list on every missing-key lookup, and ensure_loaded! calls it again on every request via set_locale. This adds avoidable work on a hot path. Memoizing the value, or invalidating it when default_locale changes, would avoid repeated lookups.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! runs on every request
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called in set_locale for every request. It walks the fallback list and calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for each locale, which takes the LOAD_MUTEX path when a locale is not yet marked loaded. The work is cheap once loaded, but it repeats the SiteSetting read and array construction on every request. Loading could happen once per locale instead of per request.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so cached results can be stale
findings.body: The LRU cache key is built from key, config.locale and the backend object_id only. With fallbacks now dependent on SiteSetting.default_locale, a translation resolved through the fallback chain is cached under a key that does not include the default locale. If default_locale changes at runtime, previously cached fallback results keep being served for that process until reload!. The key also concatenates without a separator, so distinct (key, locale) pairs can collide, for example key 'a' with locale 'en' versus key 'ae' with locale ''.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! relies on I18n.locale being a Symbol for the fallback lookup
findings.body: ensure_loaded! calls self[I18n.locale], which builds [locale, default.to_sym, :en]. If I18n.locale is ever a String, the list contains both 'en' and :en, so the same locale can be loaded twice, and the uniq does not dedupe them. The code assumes symbols everywhere without normalizing the input.

findings.title: Fallback behaviour is not covered by any test
findings.body: The PR changes global I18n fallback configuration, removes the Rails i18n.fallbacks config from three environment files, deletes the pluralization initializer, and adds a per-request loading hook. No spec exercises the fallback chain (user locale, then site default, then :en), missing-key behaviour, or the interaction with the accelerator's lazy loading. Regressions here would only surface in production.

findings.title: Deletion of the pluralization initializer is not mentioned in the PR
findings.body: The pluralization initializer is removed and its include moved into the new i18n.rb. The PR description is just 'Test 9' and does not explain this move, the removal of config.i18n.fallbacks from three environment files, or the behaviour change. Reviewers cannot verify intent from the PR text.
